title: Add root-cause default and 2026-10-13 BRIEF addendum
summary: Append a dated 2026-10-13 addendum to BRIEF.md quoting Sri verbatim ('Have Athena favor fixing root causes'), and add a `root-cause` entry to defaults.toml citing it. The entry says to fix where the fault originates, name and propose out-of-scope root causes, relate to `small`, and require fix descriptions to name the root cause and why the change addresses it.

defaults_applied.how: One focused change: two governance/spec files edited, nothing else.
The entry's wording is plain and self-contained for an outside reader.
The entry cites the BRIEF.md addendum as its source, and the quote is verbatim.
The addendum names Sri only as the existing addenda do, with no email or personal data.
The rule is prose-only for now; the entry or the summary should say so, with the verifier check as the enforcement point.
cargo test, clippy and fmt --check confirm the files still parse and the budgets hold.

assumptions: Version stays at 1: this is a new entry, not a change to an existing one. Version bumping is not asked for.
The verifiability requirement goes in the statement, so the verifier's brief carries it. Only defaults the reader names reach the producer and verifier.
Addendum format follows earlier ones: a '### 2026-10-13: Title' heading plus a bullet quoting Sri.
No Rust code change is needed because defaults.rs parses entries generically.

acceptance_criteria.text: BRIEF.md ends the Addenda section with a new '### 2026-10-13: ...' heading, after the existing 'Athena owns acceleration' addendum and without altering earlier text, quoting Sri verbatim: 'Have Athena favor fixing root causes'.
defaults.toml gains one [[default]] with a kebab-case id (e.g. 'root-cause'), a source naming the new BRIEF.md 2026-10-13 addendum, and a sensible applies_to (e.g. code, tests, config, build, docs).

The statement says: when a request reports a failure, find where the fault originates and fix it there, not the symptom or the one instance that surfaced; when the root cause is outside the request's scope, name it and propose the fix instead of silently working around it.

The entry (statement or a comment beside it) says how it relates to 'small': the root-cause fix is the one focused change; widening scope is not allowed, so out-of-scope causes are reported, not fixed. The 'small' entry is unchanged.
The entry makes the rule checkable: a fix's description must name the root cause and say why the change addresses it.

Run `cargo test` and confirm it passes. This includes the defaults.toml parse tests and the budget tests that include defaults.toml. Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` and confirm both are clean.
No files other than the listed deliverables change; records/ is untouched.

out_of_scope: Changing prompts or code to enforce the rule mechanically
departures: Smaller than typical: two text-file edits with no code. Cost and time are lowered a little. Pass probability is slightly raised, but the multi-part wording keeps some risk.
